problem: What is the order of the ordinary differential equation $x\frac{{\text{d}}^{3}y}{\text{d}{x}^{3}}-{y}^{2}\frac{{\text{d}}^{4}y}{\text{d}{x}^{4}}={y}^{5}?$

feedback.problem: What is the order of the ordinary differential equation $\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+{x}^{3}y=5{y}^{4}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}?$
feedback.worked_solution:
The order of an ordinary differential equation (ODE) is the order of the highest derivative in the equation.

The highest derivative in the given ODE is $\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}},$ which has order $2.$

Therefore, the order of the ODE is $2.$
